Definition: from G4862 and θρύπτω (to crumble); to crush together, i.e. (figuratively) to dispirit:--break.
BiblicalUsage: Paul answers, What do you mean to weep and to break my heart? For I am ready not to be bound only, but also to die at Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus. Their weeping crushes his heart, and the crushing is love itself: the tears of friends are the hardest weight a ready man has to carry.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe love can break a heart that chains cannot, and I hold that Paul's readiness to die is the measure of his love for the Lord's name.
